newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: U.N. official criticises Cambodian rights record.
newsitem.headline: U.N. official criticises Cambodian rights record.

text.p: U.N. rights official Thomas Hammarberg expressed disappointment on Wednesday over Cambodia's lack of progress on human rights issues, and said the government had failed to live up to promises to improve its record.
"There are efforts, but it is not sufficient. There is a widening gap between words and deeds," Hammarberg said on his arrival in Cambodia for a two-week mission.
He said he had formally outlined the concerns in a report expected to be delivered to the United Nations Commission on Human Rights this week.

Hammarberg, the special representative of the U.N. Secretary-General for Human Rights in Cambodia, told reporters that co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen "have (made promises) about moves which have not taken place."
He criticised the government's lack of action on earlier recommendations to remove impunity for civil servants and speed up preparations for local and national elections scheduled for 1997 and 1998.

"The national elections should be held next year... If they don't do that, it's a very negative signal for the rights to participation of the population," Hammarberg said, adding that delays in setting up the necessary laws and bodies were "quite a problem."

Hammarberg said he would investigate those topics, as well as alleged incidents of police torturing suspects, violence against journalists, child labour and the state of the education system during his two-week mission.

He will also spend four days in Battambang, Cambodia's second largest city and site of recent skirmishes between feuding government factions loyal to either Hun Sen or Ranariddh, who lead the two parties in the ruling coalition.
